report:
CONTRAST-ENHANCED CRANIAL MRI examination:
Technique: Axial plane FSE T2 and FLAIR T2, coronal plane FSE T1 and sagittal plane FSE T2, 3D BRAVO after IV contrast agent injection.

Examination:
    Bony structures and subgaleal tissue within the field of view are normal.
    In the evaluation of craniofacial region structures; nasal cavity, paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are normal.
    In the evaluation of orbits within the field of view; globes, extraorbital muscles, retrobulbar fat tissue and optic nerves were evaluated as normal.

    In posterior fossa series; the fourth ventricle is in normal location, shape and width. Cerebellar hemispheres are observed symmetrically, gray-white matter differentiation shows no abnormality.
    Pathological contrast enhancement was not detected after IV contrast agent injection.
    Brainstem structures, pons and midbrain are normal.
    Basal cisterns were observed as open.

    In supratentorial series; white and gray matter intensities in both hemispheres are observed as normal. Ventricular system is symmetrical on the midline, width is compatible with age.
    In periventricular white matter, hyperintense plaques, some of which are perpendicular to the corpus callosum, are observed on T2-weighted images. When compared with the examination dated [date_1], no significant change was observed during follow-up. Pathological contrast enhancement was not detected after IV contrast agent injection.
    Basal ganglia and thalami are normal.

Impression: Multiple plaques in periventricular white matter (No follow-up change was observed)
